title: Two ideal decay tracers limit age-spectrum oxygen ambiguity to 7.01 umol/kg for each fixed law in a tested family
abstract: We tested which ideal tracer measurements bound oxygen uncertainty when the oxygen-use time scale is not fixed in advance. We used northern hemisphere CFC-12 and SF6 input histories and constructed age spectra from zero to 100 years at 2021.5. Oxygen use had a scale of 90 umol/kg and a decay time from 3 to 30 years. Each tracer had a 0.005 source-normalized error bound. CFC-12 and SF6 permit a 54.136 umol/kg oxygen difference between spectra under one common law. A finite candidate search selected added constant-source decay tracers with e-folding times of 3 and 20 years. They reduced the attained gap to 6.798 umol/kg. Dual certificates and interpolation bounds give a continuous-age and continuous-law upper bound of 7.008 umol/kg. A proof extends the same bound to every common positive mixture of the allowed laws. Exact mean age made almost no change to the family maximum. Source uncertainty weakens the design benefit. The bound compares spectra under the same law. If the law can differ, identical spectra can give a 62.715 umol/kg difference. Thus the design controls transport-related ambiguity in this model but does not identify respiration. The decay tracers are ideal benchmarks, not demonstrated field options. Free spectra, fixed source assumptions and age-only oxygen use limit the result. Code, all search results, certificates, witnesses and numerical audits are included.
